record.title: The chromatic-plus-one conjecture for additive coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number. An additive coloring modulo $m$ assigns elements of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ to the vertices so that adjacent vertices have distinct sums of the labels on their neighbors.

**Chromatic-plus-one conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an additive coloring modulo

$$
\chi(G)+1.
$$

If true, this would be best possible, as shown in the paper. The conjecture is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Tomasz Bartnicki, Bartłomiej Bosek, Sebastian Czerwiński, Jarosław Grytczuk, Grzegorz Matecki and Wiktor Żelazny, “Additive colorings of planar graphs”, arXiv:1202.0667 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.0667

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2012). “We conclude the paper with a short list of open questions concerning additive coloring of graphs.”

record.title: The distinct-neighborhood antimagic labeling conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $N(v)$ denote the neighborhood of a vertex $v$. Assume that no two vertices have the same neighborhood.

**Distinct-neighborhood antimagic labeling conjecture.** There is a bijection $f:V(G)\rightarrow \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ such that

$$
\sum_{x\in N(u)}f(x)\neq\sum_{x\in N(v)}f(x)
$$

for any two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$.

This is introduced as a vertex analogue of the antimagic labeling conjecture of Ringel. The paper gives no resolution, so the problem remains open.
record.source_name: Tomasz Bartnicki, Bartłomiej Bosek, Sebastian Czerwiński, Jarosław Grytczuk, Grzegorz Matecki and Wiktor Żelazny, “Additive colorings of planar graphs”, arXiv:1202.0667 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.0667

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2012). “We conclude the paper with a short list of open questions concerning additive coloring of graphs.”

record.title: Hamilton decomposition conjecture for regular tripartite tournaments
record.statement:
A **tripartite tournament** is an orientation of a complete tripartite graph. It is **regular** when all vertex classes have equal size and every vertex has equal indegree and outdegree. A Hamilton decomposition is a decomposition of its arcs into directed Hamilton cycles.

**Tripartite tournament conjecture.** Every regular tripartite tournament has a Hamilton decomposition.

The paper proves the corresponding result for regular $k$-partite tournaments with $k\ge 4$ and explicitly conjectures that it extends to all $k\ge 2$. The tripartite case is therefore the first unresolved case beyond the proven range.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Hamilton decompositions of regular expanders: applications”, arXiv:1203.0659 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0659

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2012). “So in combination with , this implies that the conjecture remains open only in the case when $p$ tends to $1$ fairly quickly, i.e. when $p \ge 1-n^{-1/4} (\log n)^9$.”

record.title: Closed-form enumeration conjecture for maximal dominant weights of affine sl(n)-modules
record.statement:
Let $V(k\Lambda_0)$ be the integrable highest weight $\widehat{sl}(n)$-module, with $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$. A maximal dominant weight is a dominant weight in $V(k\Lambda_0)$ that is maximal with respect to subtraction of positive roots.

**Enumeration conjecture.** For fixed $n\geq 2$, the number of maximal dominant weights of $V(k\Lambda_0)$ is

$$
\frac{1}{n+k}\sum_{d\mid\gcd(n,k)}\phi(d)\binom{(n+k)/d}{k/d},
$$

where $\phi$ is the Euler phi function.

The formula gives a closed-form count for the maximal dominant weights. The source states that it is proved for $k\leq 3$, while the general case is presented as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Rebecca L. Jayne and Kailash C. Misra, “On multiplicities of maximal weights of sl(n)-modules”, arXiv:1309.4969 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.4969

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

record.title: Ahlfors extremals realizing the gonality
record.statement: Let a compact bordered Riemann surface have gonality equal to the least degree of a conformal map to the disc, and let $f_{a,b}$ denote an Ahlfors extremal function associated with two marked points, with $f_a$ the limiting one-point extremal. **Ahlfors gonality conjecture.** Any conformal mapping realizing the gonality arises as an Ahlfors extremal function $f_{a,b}$, perhaps after coalescing two points to obtain an Ahlfors map $f_a$ maximizing the modulus of the derivative at $a$. The source records the question as unsettled; it is proved there only in the hyperelliptic case.
record.source_name: Alexandre Gabard, “Notes on Hilbert's 16th: experiencing Viro's theory”, arXiv:1310.1865 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1865

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: Caputo's shuffle spectral gap conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n\ge 3$. For each $A\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $S_{n,A}$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ fixing every element outside $A$, and define

$$
J_{n,A}:=\sum_{\pi\in S_{n,A}}\pi.
$$

For nonnegative coefficients $\alpha_A$, set

$$
w=\sum_{A\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}}\alpha_AJ_{n,A}.
$$

Let $\operatorname{supp}w$ denote the support of $w$, and let $\psi_{S_n}(w)$ be the spectral gap of $w$, while $\psi_{S_n}(w,\mathsf D)$ is the spectral gap in the representation $\mathsf D$. **Caputo's conjecture.** If $\operatorname{supp}w$ generates $S_n$, then

$$
\psi_{S_n}(w)=\psi_{S_n}(w,\mathsf D).
$$

This conjecture was communicated privately by P. Caputo, and the source reports that it resisted both proof attempts and numerical disproof; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Filippo Cesi, “A few remarks on the octopus inequality and Aldous' spectral gap conjecture”, arXiv:1310.6156 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.6156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: Elekes's uniform statistical conjecture for small image sets of lines
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the set of lines under consideration. For sets $\Phi\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ and $H\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ of size at least $n$, let $E\subseteq\Phi\times H$ define a bipartite graph $G(\Phi,H,E)$, and write

$$
\Phi_E(H)=\{\phi(h):(\phi,h)\in E\}.
$$

A family of lines is **parallel** if all its lines are parallel, and a **star family** if all its lines pass through one point. **Elekes's conjecture.** For fixed $\alpha>0$, if every $\phi\in\Phi$ has degree at least $\alpha n$ in $G(\Phi,H,E)$ and

$$
|\Phi_E(H)|\leq Cn,
$$

then $\Phi$ is the union of a constant number of parallel and star families. This is a uniform statistical form of the small-image-set theorem for lines; the source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: G. Amirkhanyan, A. Bush, E. Croot and C. Pryby, “Sets of Rich Lines in General Position”, arXiv:1310.6707 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.6707

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: Batyrev–Nill codegree conjecture for Cayley decompositions
record.statement:
For a lattice polytope $P$, define its **codegree** by

$$
\operatorname{codeg}(P)=\min_{\mathbb Z}\{t\mid tP\text{ has interior lattice points}\}.
$$

For example, the unimodular simplex satisfies $\operatorname{codeg}(\Delta_n)=n+1$. **Batyrev–Nill conjecture.** There is a function $f(n)$ such that every $n$-dimensional polytope $P$ with $\operatorname{codeg}(P)\geqslant f(n)$ decomposes as a Cayley sum of lattice polytopes. This conjecture concerns the relationship between large codegree and Cayley-sum structure; it was later proven by Haase, Nill, and Payne, who showed in addition that $f(n)$ is at most quadratic in $n$.
record.source_name: Sandra Di Rocco, “Linear Toric Fibrations”, arXiv:1311.1625 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1625

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2013). “The above conjecture was proven by Haase, Nill and Payne in .”

record.title: The quadratic conjecture for 3-connected matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a $3$-connected matroid, and let $J_M$ be its toric ideal. **3-connected quadratic conjecture.** For any $3$-connected matroid $M$,

1. $J_M$ is generated by quadratic binomials.
2. $J_M$ has a quadratic Gröbner basis.

The source presents these assertions as sufficient for proving the preceding equality conjecture, because non-3-connected matroids can be constructed from 3-connected proper minors by direct sums and 2-sums. They remain open in the generality stated.
record.source_name: Kazuki Shibata, “Toric ideals of series and parallel connections of matroids”, arXiv:1312.3428 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3428

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Serre's domination by maximal motives conjecture
record.statement:
Let $E$ be a motive over $K$, and let $G_{\mathcal{M}(E)}$ denote its motivic Galois group. **Serre's domination by maximal motives conjecture.** After replacing $K$ by a finite extension, there exists a maximal motive $E'$ dominating $E$ such that

$$
G_{\mathcal{M}(E')}\longrightarrow G_{\mathcal{M}(E)}
$$

is a connected covering. This conjecture proposes that every motive becomes dominated by a maximal one after a finite base-field extension; its status is open in general.
record.source_name: Chun Yin Hui and Michael Larsen, “Adelic openness without the Mumford-Tate conjecture”, arXiv:1312.3812 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3812

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Munson–Volić collapse conjecture for the long-link spectral sequence
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{K}^{m\bullet}_d$ be the cosimplicial space of long links of $m$ strands in $\mathbb{R}^d$ constructed by Munson and Volić, and let its homology Bousfield–Kan spectral sequence converge to $H_*(\overline{\mathcal{L}}_m^d;\mathbb{Q})$. **Munson–Volić's conjecture.** This spectral sequence collapses at the $E^2$ page rationally for $d\geq 4$. The paper states that its main result proves this conjecture, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Paul Arnaud Songhafouo Tsopméné, “The rational homology of spaces of long links”, arXiv:1312.7280 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7280

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Peng–Zhao Motzkin–Straus-type conjecture for hypergraphs with a large clique
record.statement:
Let $t$, $m$, and $r\ge 3$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\binom{t-1}{r}\le m\le\binom{t-1}{r}+\binom{t-2}{r-1}.
$$

Let $G$ be an $r$-graph with $m$ edges that contains a clique of order $t-1$. **Peng–Zhao's Motzkin–Straus-type conjecture.** Then

$$
\lambda(G)=\lambda([t-1]^{(r)}).
$$

The upper bound is best possible, as the source gives an $(r,m)$-graph with one additional edge whose Lagrangian exceeds that of $[t-1]^{(r)}$. The conjecture concerns the relationship between clique number and Lagrangian and is presented as a conjecture attributed to Peng and Zhao; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Qingsong Tang, Yuejian Peng, Xiangde Zhang and Cheng Zhao, “Connection between the clique number and the Lagrangian of 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1312.7529 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7529

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Rasmussen's spectral sequence conjecture from reduced Khovanov homology to knot Floer homology
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. Denote by $\overline{Kh}(K)$ the reduced Khovanov homology of $K$, and by $\widehat{\mathit{HFK}}(K)$ the reduced, delta-graded knot Floer homology of $K$.

**Rasmussen's spectral sequence conjecture.** There is a spectral sequence from $\overline{Kh}(K)$ to $\widehat{\mathit{HFK}}(K)$.

This conjecture is one of the central proposed connections between Khovanov homology and Heegaard Floer homology. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Nathan Dowlin, “A family of sl_n-like invariants in knot Floer homology”, arXiv:1804.03165 (2018).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1310.3418](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3418).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.03165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: The Gröbner basis characterization of 0- and 1-inductively pierced codes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a code on $n$ neurons, and let $I_{\mathcal{C}}$ be its toric ideal. A **reduced Gröbner basis** is the unique reduced Gröbner basis of $I_{\mathcal{C}}$ with respect to a chosen monomial order.

**The Gröbner basis characterization.** For each $n$, there exists a monomial order such that $\mathcal{C}$ is $0$- or $1$-inductively pierced if and only if the reduced Gröbner basis of $I_{\mathcal{C}}$ contains only binomials of degree at most $2$.

This conjecture seeks a Gröbner-theoretic characterization of low-order inductive piercing for combinatorial neural codes, extending the stated result for codes on three neurons. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Melissa Beer, Robert Davis, Thomas Elgin, Matthew Hertel, Kira Laws, Rajinder Mavi, Paula Mercurio and Alexandra Newlon, “Universal Gröbner Bases of Toric Ideals of Combinatorial Neural Codes”, arXiv:1904.10127 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1308.2632](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.2632).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10127

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Bipartite Ramsey number conjecture for two copies of $K_{2,n}$
record.statement:
For integers $n\geq 2$, let $m_n(K_{2,n},K_{2,n})$ denote the corresponding bipartite Ramsey number for two copies of $K_{2,n}$, as used in the paper. The known value is $m_2(K_{2,2},K_{2,2})=5$, and the paper discusses the same value for larger even parameters.

**Bipartite Ramsey number conjecture for two copies of $K_{2,n}$.**

$$
m_n(K_{2,n},K_{2,n})=5\quad\text{for }n\geq 2.
$$

This would extend the known case $n=2$ and the cited result for the relevant odd prime-power cases to all $n\geq 2$; the even values beyond $n=2$ are presented as unresolved.
record.source_name: I Wayan Palton Anuwiksa, Rinovia Simanjuntak and Edy Tri Baskoro, “Multipartite Ramsey numbers of complete bipartite graphs arising from algebraic combinatorial structures”, arXiv:2307.09736 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1303.5475](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.5475).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09736

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “Finally, we conclude by proposing some open problems in Section .”

record.title: Discrete Fourier restriction conjecture for the monomial curve
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$ be an integer, let $N\in\mathbb N$, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb C$, and write $\mathbb T^2$ for the two-dimensional torus. For $p\geq 2(d+1)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, **the discrete Fourier restriction conjecture** asserts that

$$
\left\|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n e^{2\pi i x_1 n+2\pi i x_2 n^d}\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb T^2)}\lesssim N^\varepsilon\left(\sum_{n=1}^N|a_n|^2\right)^{\frac12}.
$$

This is a mean-value estimate for exponential sums on the discrete curve $(n,n^d)$ and is of interest in additive number theory because it would yield a substantial improvement in Waring's problem. It is also a discrete Fourier restriction problem; the source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Xiaochun Li, “A Stein-Tomas type estimate and a decoupling inequality”, arXiv:2309.12835 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1310.5244](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5244).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.12835

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Norine's conjecture on monochromatic antipodal paths in cube graphs
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional cube graph, whose vertices are binary strings of length $n$. For a vertex $u$, write $\bar u$ for the vertex obtained by complementing every bit, and call $u$ and $\bar u$ **antipodal**. An **antipodal edge-coloring** of $Q_n$ is a red/blue edge-coloring in which every pair of antipodal edges has different colors.

**Norine's conjecture.** For $n\ge 2$, any antipodal edge-coloring of $Q_n$ contains antipodal vertices $u$ and $\bar u$ such that $u$ and $\bar u$ are joined by a monochromatic path.

Previous work had proved the conjecture for $n\le 6$, and this paper verifies it for $n=7$ using SAT solvers. The conjecture concerns the existence of a monochromatic connection between antipodal vertices, although the path need not be geodesic.
record.source_name: Keith Frankston and Danny Scheinerman, “Proving Norine's Conjecture holds for n=7 via SAT solvers”, arXiv:2408.02474 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1301.2195](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2195).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02474

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Rank-unimodality conjecture for principal permutation-pattern downsets
record.statement: Let $\rho$ be a permutation, and let $D(\rho)$ be the principal downset of all permutations contained in $\rho$, ordered by permutation-pattern containment and ranked by permutation length. A ranked poset is rank-unimodal when its rank sizes form a unimodal sequence. **Rank-unimodality conjecture for principal downsets.** Every principal downset in the permutation pattern poset is rank-unimodal. This is presented as an unresolved unimodality problem; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Vincent Vatter, “An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting”, arXiv:2602.16355 (2026).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2108.12979](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12979), [arXiv:1403.1527](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1527), [arXiv:1305.5569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.5569).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: Feder–Subi conjecture on antipodal paths with few colour changes
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$) be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, with edge set $E(Q_n)$, and consider a 2-colouring of its edges. Two vertices are **antipodal** if they differ in every coordinate.

**Feder–Subi conjecture.** Every 2-colouring of $E(Q_n)$ contains a path between some pair of antipodal vertices which changes colour at most once.

This strengthens Norine's conjecture, which asks only for a monochromatic path between some pair of antipodal vertices. The conjecture was proved in according to the supplied status evidence.
record.source_name: Lawrence Hollom, “Hypercube geodesics with few colour changes”, arXiv:2605.20184 (2026).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1504.05987](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.05987), [arXiv:1301.2195](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2195).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20184

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Quadratic bound conjecture for products of primitive matrices
record.statement:
Let a set of primitive matrices of dimension $n$ satisfy Assumption 1, namely the nonzero-row, nonzero-column condition stated in the paper. A product of matrices is called **positive** when all its entries are positive.

**Quadratic bound conjecture.** There is a constant $K$ such that every such set has a product of length smaller than $Kn^2$ with positive entries.

This conjecture asks whether the general cubic upper bound can be reduced to quadratic order. The preceding discussion notes that the cubic bound is not known to be sharp; the status of the quadratic bound remains open.
record.source_name: Vincent D. Blondel, Raphael M. Jungers and Alex Olshevsky, “On Primitivity of Sets of Matrices”, arXiv:1306.0729 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0729

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).
